_comment: The course manifest: the single source of the structure. The build reads it to produce every page, the menus, the figure numbers, previous/next links and the sitemap. Beats are named by the id of the figure they carry (the internal data-fig id, which never changes); a beat is moved whole, with its text. 'tails' says where each old module's closing elements go (recap, bridge, Go deeper panels, mathematics panel, source list). Titles follow the restructuring plan (Titles and headings).
title: How batteries work
subtitle: The electrochemistry of lithium-ion cells, from first principles to the laboratory

parts.title: Foundations: electrostatics and the electrochemical cell
Cell operation: galvanostatic cycling, polarization and voltage profiles
Inside the cell: insertion hosts, ion transport and interfaces
Materials: electrodes, solid electrolytes and emerging chemistries
Degradation, safety and end of life

pages.title: Electrostatics for electrochemistry: charge, field, potential and current
pages.question: A torch cell says 1.5 V on its side. What is a volt, and what is being pushed?

pages.seo_desc: Coulomb's law, electric field, potential and why a current needs a voltage, explained with interactive figures as the basis for how batteries work.

pages.seo_desc: What is inside a lithium-ion battery: electrodes, separator, electrolyte, current collectors, the four cell formats and the rocking-chair principle.

pages.seo_title: Battery capacity, energy, C-rate and power explained

pages.title: Insertion hosts: intercalation, alloying and conversion reactions

pages.seo_desc: Where lithium is stored in a battery: intercalation into graphite and LiCoO2, staging, alloying with silicon and conversion reactions.

pages.seo_title: Ion transport in batteries: diffusion, migration, transference
